title: Grade 5 Science — Tue, Jun 02
description: The Skeletal System — Day 2 of 5: Joints and how we bend
subject: science

questions.question: The place where two bones meet is called a:
questions.explanation: A joint is the point where two or more bones meet, allowing movement.

questions.question: The joint at the elbow allows movement in only one direction, like a door. It is a:
questions.explanation: The elbow is a hinge joint that bends in only one direction, like a door hinge.

questions.question: The shoulder joint can move in many directions. It is a:
questions.explanation: The shoulder is a ball-and-socket joint, allowing the arm to move in many directions.

questions.question: Which of these is also a hinge joint?
questions.explanation: The knee is a hinge joint that bends back and forth in one direction.

questions.question: The joints in the skull do NOT move. They are called:
questions.explanation: The bones of the skull are joined by fixed (immovable) joints.

questions.question: The joint in the neck that lets us turn our head side to side is a:
questions.explanation: The pivot joint in the neck allows the head to rotate from side to side.

questions.question: Joints are important because they allow our body to:
questions.explanation: Joints make it possible for parts of the body to bend, turn and move.

questions.question: Which joint lets you rotate your arm in a full circle?
questions.explanation: The ball-and-socket joint of the shoulder lets the arm move in a full circle.

questions.question: Why can't you bend your knee backwards far?
options: It is a hinge joint that moves only one way
questions.explanation: The knee is a hinge joint, so it bends mainly in one direction.

questions.question: Bones at a joint are held together by tough bands called:
questions.explanation: Ligaments are strong bands that hold the bones together at a joint.

questions.question: The hip joint, like the shoulder, is a:
questions.explanation: The hip is a ball-and-socket joint, allowing the leg to move in many directions.

questions.question: Which everyday action uses a hinge joint?
questions.explanation: Bending the elbow uses a hinge joint, which moves in one direction.

questions.question: Fixed joints in the skull are useful because they:
options: Hold the skull bones firmly to protect the brain
questions.explanation: Fixed joints lock the skull bones together to form a strong case for the brain.

questions.question: Which list shows joints from most movable to least movable?
questions.explanation: The shoulder (ball-and-socket) moves most, the elbow (hinge) less, and skull joints are fixed.

questions.question: Without joints, our arms and legs would be:
questions.explanation: Joints allow bending; without them our limbs would be stiff and could not move.
